title: μπ, ντ and γκ: b, d and g

steps.text: Greek has no letter for b, d or the g of “go”: it writes them with two letters, μπ, ντ and γκ; and γγ is always ng. An English reader sees mp, nt and nk and says them so: πάντα as “panta”. Inside a word Lampas says them mb, nd and ng, as in “number”, “under” and “finger”: πάντα is “panda”. At the start of a word, in Greek as it is spoken today, they are a plain b, d and g; but no word of the New Testament starts with them.

Say “number”, “under” and “finger”. The m, the n and the ng run straight into a b, a d or a g, with the voice going all the way through: that is μπ, ντ and γκ inside a word. Now say “panda”, and you have said πάντα.
Listen to the voice go through each pair: ντ is nd in ἐντολή and πάντα, γγ is ng in ἀγγελία and ἄγγελος, μπ is mb in ἔμπροσθεν. None is a t, a p or a k.
In each pair one word has τ or ν alone, the other the pair: τ is a clean t and ντ is nd; ν is n, and γκ and γγ are ng. Hear both words, then say both.
Say each word after the voice. Let the voice run through the pair with no break and no puff: ἐντολή is “en-do-LEE”, never “en-to-LEE”.
An old commandment: ἐντολή three times, each ντ marked. Hear it, then say it, nd every time.
